text: The retrieved list is thin and mostly off-topic for these hypotheses. It contains no experimental or survey findings on how information type, tie strength, sharer trust, ideology, knowledge or conspiracy belief affect sharing or perceived plausibility of misinformation, so it cannot support or contextualize H1-H14, the reweighted robustness checks R1-R12, or the exploratory analyses X1-X13. The only directly relevant item is a general review of fake news, disinformation and misinformation on social media [citation removed: not in retrieved set], whose snippet gives no specific findings. A review of prejudice toward immigrants (Esses, 2020) is only loosely related to the sharer-origin hypotheses (H3, H10, X13). Its snippet reports no findings on how sharer origin affects information sharing or credibility, so I draw no conclusions from it.
